analysis.title: What Matters Today: US Rates Lower on Hot Inflation Prints, A Higher Cost of Capital for AI Credit, Warsh Hints at Pausing in October, Hedge Fund Pain Yesterday
key_insights: US rates caught a bid on 10/15 and held overnight despite a hot CPI and a hot PPI. The author notes some nuance in PPI composition, particularly energy, but calls the underlying print robust.

The author argues rates are starting to reflect the same AI capex growth shock equities have repriced this week. If AI capex disappoints, growth expectations fall and bonds rally. If spending meets expectations, growth stays robust and yields probably rise.

The author says too much capital is chasing too little investable, energized compute. Repricing may be gradual or acute and could become systemic. Scarcity of available compute is structurally bullish for those who already own it.

The author expects robust hyperscaler earnings and asks whether the free cash flow inflection could be pulled forward materially, reducing the need for incremental leverage. Hyperscalers keep financial flexibility given resilient equity valuations.

USD HY AI-related spreads widened 25bp between Oct 13 and 14 to a new high of 360bp over Treasuries. Non-AI HY spreads were only 2bp wider and remain below their March peak. USD IG AI-related spreads were 3bp wider.

GS remains underweight USD IG Technology and neutral USD HY. It sees scope for a near-term reversal of the sell-off and more attractive valuations in HY, but expects dispersion across AI-related issuers to stay high.

Project finance issuance in USD IG and HY has passed $106B, nearly three times the full-year 2025 level of $37B. GS expects $300B of global project finance issuance in 2027 for data centers and compute, on top of $420B of direct hyperscaler issuance it forecasts for next year.

Fed Chairman Warsh at the IMF meetings did not address the October FOMC directly but said the world has broadly conformed to the FOMC's expectations since the September meeting. GS reads this, with other FOMC comments, as a pause in October and still expects a second and final hike in December.
Odds of an October hike fell from about 30% to about 17% after the remarks. The Fed enters its blackout period on 10/17.
Hedge fund performance on 10/15 was weak: momentum fell further and crowding hurt more, with losses concentrated in quants and a small recovery in fundamental managers.

trade_ideas.rationale: AI-related spread widening and large expected issuance for data center and compute funding.

risk_factors: AI capex disappointing would lower growth expectations, and the repricing in AI assets could become systemic.
Heavy AI-related debt supply: $300B project finance and $420B hyperscaler issuance expected in 2027.
Dispersion across AI-related credit issuers is likely to remain high.
Crowded momentum positioning is generating hedge fund losses.
vol_and_positioning: Global Fundamental L/S managers fell 0.5% (-0.8 SD move) on 10/15 and are up 10% YTD.
Global Systematic L/S managers fell 1.4% (-3.7 SD), the worst day since Aug 19, and are still up 20% YTD.
Multi-strat managers (equity portfolio, 4.5x leverage) fell 1.2% (-2.2 SD).
Momentum fell further and crowding hurt more, with pain across quants.

tension_points.bull_case: If AI spending meets expectations, growth remains robust, and hyperscaler earnings and an earlier free cash flow inflection could ease financing concerns.
tension_points.bear_case: If AI capex disappoints, growth expectations fall and bonds rally. Too much capital chasing scarce compute could drive a repricing that becomes systemic.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler earnings that show an earlier free cash flow inflection and less need for leverage would undercut the funding-stress view.
